Ang talino mo! Ang maikling simbolo na ginagamit natin para sa kilometro ay "km". Madaling tandaan!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mubo nga simbolo nga atong gigamit para sa kilometro?

Kaalam ka! Ang mubo nga simbolo nga atong gigamit para sa kilometro kay "km". Sayon hinumdoman!

Kingdom Protista is made up of tiny living things like the amoeba, most of which live in water.

Ang kahariang Protista ay binubuo ng maliliit na organismo gaya ng ameba, na karaniwang nabubuhay sa tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gingharian nga Protista?

Ang gingharian nga Protista gilangkob sa gagmayng organismo sama sa amoeba, nga kasagaran nagpuyo sa tubig.

After beating the fish on a branch, it swallows head-first so the scales don't catch in its throat.

Matapos ibagsak ang isda sa sanga, nilulunok ito ng kingfisher nang paulo muna para hindi masakal sa kaliskis.

What's the largest lizard in the world?

The Komodo dragon of Indonesia! It's a giant monitor lizard, related to our bayawak but not found here.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking butiki sa mundo?

Ang Komodo dragon ng Indonesia! Higanteng monitor lizard ito, kamag-anak ng ating bayawak pero hindi matatagpuan dito.
copy.bis:
Unsay pinakadakong tiki sa kalibutan?

Ang Komodo dragon sa Indonesia! Higante nga monitor lizard kini, paryente sa atong bayawak apan wala dinhi.

copy.tl: Ang batik-batik na balat ng ladybug ay matigas na takip pala — nagtatago ito ng manipis na pakpak na ginagamit nitong paglipad.

How does a ladybug scare off birds?

When scared, a ladybug oozes orange blood from its leg joints — it tastes bitter, so birds and other predators leave it alone!
copy.tl:
Paano nagtataboy ang ladybug ng ibon?

Kapag natakot, naglalabas ang ladybug ng orange na dugo mula sa kasukasuan ng binti nito — mapait ito kaya iniiwasan siya ng ibon at iba pang mandaragit!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-abog sa ladybug sa langgam?

Kung mahadlok, naglabas ang ladybug og orange nga dugo gikan sa kasukasuan sa iyang tiil — mapait kini mao nga likayan siya sa langgam ug uban pang manunukob!

May mga pagong sa lupa na naitalang nabuhay nang halos 180 taon, kabilang sa pinakamatandang hayop sa mundo!
copy.bis:
Hangtod kanus-a mabuhi ang baw-i sa yuta?

Ang ubang mga baw-i sa yuta narekord nga nabuhi og halos 180 ka tuig, usa sa labing tigulang nga mga hayop!

The lanternfish! It's among the most abundant fish anywhere in the deep sea, found all over the world's oceans.

Anong isda ang sagana sa malalim na dagat?

Ang lanternfish! Isa ito sa pinakamaraming uri ng isda sa malalim na dagat sa buong mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsang isda ang daghan kaayo sa lawom nga dagat?

Ang lanternfish! Usa kini sa labing daghan nga matang sa isda sa lawom nga dagat sa tibuok kalibutan.

Spinosaurus was the largest meat-eating dinosaur ever — even bigger than the famous Tyrannosaurus rex!
copy.tl:

Ang Spinosaurus ang pinakamalaking dinosaur na kumakain ng karne — mas malaki pa ito kaysa sikat na Tyrannosaurus rex!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga dinosaur nga mokaon og karne?

Ang Spinosaurus mao ang pinakadako nga dinosaur nga mokaon og karne — mas dako pa kini kay sa bantog nga Tyrannosaurus rex!

What is the biggest tree in the world?

The biggest tree in the world by trunk size is a giant sequoia named General Sherman!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking puno sa mundo?

Ang pinakamalaking puno sa mundo ayon sa laki ng katawan ay isang giant sequoia na tinatawag na General Sherman!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadako nga kahoy sa kalibutan?

Ang pinakadako nga kahoy sa kalibutan basi sa gidak-on sa lawas kay usa ka giant sequoia nga ginganlag General Sherman!

copy.tl: Sa LASIK, ginagamit ng doktor ang laser para baguhin ang hugis ng cornea, itinatama nito ang malabong paningin kaya hindi na kailangan ng salamin.
copy.bis: Sa LASIK, gigamit sa doktor ang laser aron usbon ang porma sa cornea, matul-id niini ang hanap nga panan-aw mao nga wala nay kinahanglan nga salamin.

copy.bis: Ang latex usa ka puti nga duga nga makuha gikan sa kahoy nga gitawag og rubber tree!

How does soap clean clothes in the basin?

Soap grabs oil and dirt, mixing them into the water so they easily wash right out of your clothes!
copy.tl:
Paano naglilinis ang sabon sa batya?

Kinakapit ng sabon ang langis at dumi, at hinahalo sa tubig para madaling matanggal sa iyong mga damit!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglimpyo sa sabon sa batya?

Gakupot sa sabon ang lana ug hugaw, unya gisagol sa tubig aron sayon kining matangtang gikan sa sapot!

copy.tl: May mga dahon sa Pilipinas na ginagamit bilang gamot — halimbawa, ang dahon ng lagundi ay madalas gawing gamot sa ubo. Pero dapat may gabay pa rin ng doktor.
copy.bis: Adunay mga dahon sa Pilipinas nga gigamit isip tambal — pananglitan, ang dahon sa lagundi kasagarang himoon nga tambal sa ubo. Apan kinahanglan gihapon adunay giya sa doktor.

Why do leaves change color?

When cold weather comes, trees stop making chlorophyll, so the green fades away and the yellow and red underneath show through.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagbabago ng kulay ang mga dahon?

Kapag dumating ang malamig na panahon, huminto na ang puno sa paggawa ng chlorophyll, kaya nawawala ang berde at lumilitaw ang dilaw at pula.
copy.bis:
Nganong mausab ang kolor sa mga dahon?

Kon moabot ang bugnaw nga panahon, mohunong ang kahoy paghimo og chlorophyll, mao nga mawala ang berde ug motungha ang dalag ug pula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaves also hold yellow and orange colors, hidden by lots of green chlorophyll.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses leaf pigments and color change, not the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor raw materials and products. Chlorophyll is mentioned but only as a pigment, not in the context of photosynthesis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Leaves also hold yellow and orange colors, hidden by lots of green chlorophyll.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves but does not describe their outer parts or their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil. It is about leaf color pigments, not plant structure or function.

copy.en:
Why do leaves change color?

Leaves also hold yellow and orange colors, hidden by lots of green chlorophyll. So leaves look green while healthy, and other colors appear once the chlorophyll fades.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagbabago ng kulay ang dahon?

May iba pang kulay tulad ng dilaw at orange sa loob ng dahon, pero natatakpan ng maraming berdeng chlorophyll. Kaya berde ang dahon habang malusog, at lumilitaw ang ibang kulay kapag nawawala na ang chlorophyll.
copy.bis:
Nganong mausab ang kolor sa dahon?

Adunay laing kolor sama sa dalag ug orange sa sulod sa dahon, apan natabonan sa daghang berdeng chlorophyll. Mao nga berde ang dahon samtang himsog, ug mogawas ang laing kolor kung mawala na ang chlorophyll.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Too much heat makes bubbles and holes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat causing bubbles, but it does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation). It is about cooking texture, not state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Too much heat makes bubbles and holes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how temperature changes cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It only notes that excessive heat ruins custard texture; no state change is taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Too much heat makes bubbles and holes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to temperature changes like burning wood or coal. It is about cooking custard, not material property changes.

copy.en: Leche flan is cooked with gentle steam, not a hard boil! Too much heat makes bubbles and holes, turning the smooth custard grainy instead.
copy.tl: Ang leche flan ay niluluto sa mahinang steam, hindi sa malakas na kumukulong tubig! Sobrang init ay gumagawa ng bula at butas, kaya magaspang ang custard imbes na makinis.
copy.bis: Ang leche flan giluto sa hinay nga alisngaw, dili sa kusog nga nagbukal! Sobra nga kainit maghimo og bula ug lungag, maong magaspang ang custard imbes nga hamis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As it drinks blood, its body swells bigger and bigger.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a leech drinking blood but does not group animals by diet (herbivore/carnivore/omnivore) or use secondary sources to classify. It only touches on feeding behavior, not the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: As it drinks blood, its body swells bigger and bigger.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the leech's body swelling but does not describe outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement and gathering food. No direct support for observing/describing body parts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Once full, it just lets go and drops off
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a feeding response (letting go when full) but does not teach the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The response is specific to leech feeding, not a general characteristic lesson.

copy.en:
How does a leech know when to stop feeding?

As it drinks blood, its body swells bigger and bigger. Once full, it just lets go and drops off — sometimes after drinking more blood than it weighs!
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng linta kung kailan titigil sa pag-inom?

Habang umiinom ng dugo, lumalaki at lumulobo ang katawan nito. Kapag busog na, kusa itong bumibitaw at nahuhulog — kaya minsan nakakainom pa ito ng dugong mas marami sa sarili niyang timbang!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkahibalo sa alimatok nga mohunong na sa pagsuyop?

Samtang nagainom og dugo, modako ug mohupong ang lawas niini. Kon busog na, kusog ra kining mobuhi ug mahulog — usahay makainom pa kini og dugo nga mas daghan sa iyang kaugalingong gibug-aton!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all leeches suck blood — some eat small water animals instead!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions what leeches eat but does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to classify animals by diet. It only touches on the broad topic of animal food habits.

copy.en:
Do all leeches drink blood?

Not all leeches suck blood — some eat small water animals instead!
copy.tl:
Lahat ba ng linta, dugo lang kinakain?

Hindi lahat ng linta sumisipsip ng dugo — may mga linta na kumakain ng maliliit na hayop sa tubig!
copy.bis:
Tanan ba nga linta, dugo ra gikaon?

Dili tanang linta nagasupsop ug dugo — ang uban nagakaon hinuon og gagmayng mananap sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After just one big drink of blood, a leech can survive for many months before it needs to feed again!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions feeding but does not identify or teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It is a specific fact about leech survival, not instruction on basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: After just one big drink of blood, a leech can survive for many months before it needs to feed again!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a leech's ability to survive long between meals, which could be seen as an adaptation, but it does not describe how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it use secondary sources or provide examples like mimicry or camouflage. The connection to the competency is only thematic.

copy.en:
How long can a leech go without eating?

After just one big drink of blood, a leech can survive for many months before it needs to feed again!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal di kumain ang linta?

Pagkatapos ng isang malaking inom ng dugo, kayang mabuhay ng linta nang maraming buwan bago muling kumain!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay dili mokaon ang linta?

Human sa usa ka dako nga inom sa dugo, mabuhi ang linta sulod sa daghang bulan una mokaon pag-usab!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hot food should be cooled a little before being put in the fridge so it does not warm up the inside of the refrigerator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions hot food warming the fridge but does not explain convection or conduction using the particle model, nor does it describe any heat-transfer mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hot food should be cooled a little before being put in the fridge so it does not warm up the inside of the refrigerator!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves heat-related everyday advice but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature.

copy.en:
Why should hot food cool down before going in the fridge?

Hot food should be cooled a little before being put in the fridge so it does not warm up the inside of the refrigerator!
copy.tl:
Bakit dapat munang lumamig ang mainit na pagkain bago ilagay sa ref?

Ang mainit na pagkain ay dapat munang palamigin nang bahagya bago ilagay sa ref para hindi tumaas ang init sa loob nito!
copy.bis:
Nganong angay unang molamig ang init nga pagkaon sa dili pa ibutang sa ref?

Ang init nga pagkaon angay unang palamigon gamay sa dili pa ibutang sa ref aron dili moinit ang sulod niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pod that holds peas and beans is actually a kind of fruit from the plant.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Botanical fruit identity is adjacent to seed production; the card does not describe pollination, seed production, or propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the pod that holds peas and beans is actually a kind of fruit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: Culinary vs botanical grouping is not using a table or the listed classification groups.

copy.en:
Is the pea pod really a fruit?

Yes! The pod that holds peas and beans is actually a kind of fruit from the plant.
copy.tl:
Bunga ba talaga ang pod ng gisantes?

Oo! Ang pod na sumasakop sa buto ng gisantes at sitaw ay isang uri ng bunga ng halaman.
copy.bis:
Bunga ba gyud ang pod sa gisantes?

Oo! Ang pod nga naghawid sa liso sa gisantes ug sitaw usa ka matang sa bunga sa tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the bacteria can also be found in the urine of dogs, cattle, and pigs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria but does not teach the unicellular vs multicellular distinction. It only states that bacteria can be carried by various animals, providing no instructional support for recognizing single-celled vs multi-celled organisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the bacteria can also be found in the urine of dogs, cattle, and pigs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card notes that leptospirosis bacteria can be carried by several animals, implying potential harm through disease, but it does not explain how interactions between living things bring good or harm. It lacks the explanatory content required by the competency.

copy.en: Rats aren't the only carriers of leptospirosis, the bacteria can also be found in the urine of dogs, cattle, and pigs.
copy.tl: Hindi lang daga ang nagdadala ng bakterya ng leptospirosis, nasa ihi rin ito ng aso, baka, at baboy.
copy.bis: Dili lang ang ilaga ang nagdala sa bakterya sa leptospirosis, anaa usab kini sa ihi sa iro, baka, ug baboy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: reducing the usage time of high-power appliances lowers the total electrical energy consumption
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electrical energy consumption and cost, but does not address electricity as a flow of electrons or safe handling of electricity, which are the core actions of G9-F-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: reducing the usage time of high-power appliances lowers the total electrical energy consumption
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe and explain the need for safety precautions in handling household electrical devices
assignedReviews.reason: The card concerns household electrical devices and energy use, but it does not describe or explain safety precautions for handling household electrical devices, which is the required competency.

copy.en:
Why does my electric bill go down when I use the flat iron less?

Because reducing the usage time of high-power appliances lowers the total electrical energy consumption, which lowers the cost!
copy.tl:
Bakit bumababa ang bill ko sa kuryente kapag hindi ko masyadong ginagamit ang plantsa?

Dahil ang pagbawas sa oras ng paggamit ng mga high-power na appliance ay nagpapababa ng kabuuang konsumo ng electrical energy, kaya bumababa rin ang bayad!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mous-os ang akong bayad sa kuryente kon dili nako kanunay gamiton ang plantsa?

Tungod kay ang pagpakgang sa oras sa paggamit sa mga high-power nga appliance makapaus-os sa kinatibuk-ang konsumo sa electrical energy, mao nga mous-os usab ang bayad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Head lice spread when heads touch, or when combs, hats, or hair ties get shared between people
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: How lice spread is not explaining how an interaction brings good or harm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Head lice spread when heads touch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: Head lice spread when heads touch, or when combs, hats, or hair ties get shared between people.
copy.tl: Kumakalat ang kuto kapag nagdikit ang mga ulo, o kapag hinihiram-hiraman ang suklay, sumbrero, o gomang pambuhok.
copy.bis: Mokatap ang kuto kung magdikit ang mga ulo, o kung gibahin-bahin ang sudlay, kalo, o higot sa buhok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has no true roots, stems, or leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that lichen is not a plant because it lacks true roots, stems, or leaves, but it does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). The content is only loosely related to classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it has no true roots, stems, or leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions roots, stems, and leaves only to say lichen lacks them; it does not teach students to observe the outer parts of plants or identify their roles in getting water and nutrients. This is not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
Is lichen a plant?

No — even though lichen looks like a plant, it isn't one, because it has no true roots, stems, or leaves.
copy.tl:
Halaman ba ang lichen?

Hindi — kahit mukhang halaman ang lichen, hindi ito halaman dahil wala itong tunay na ugat, tangkay, o dahon.
copy.bis:
Tanom ba ang lichen?

Dili — bisan og daw tanom ang lichen, dili kini tanom kay wala kini tinuod nga gamot, punoan, o dahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lichens come in different forms: some look like a crust, some look like leaves, and some look like tiny branches.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes lichen growth forms (crustose, foliose, fruticose) but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms). Lichens are fungi-related, but the card provides no classification instruction or table, so it only shares vocabulary with the competency.

copy.en: Lichens come in different forms: some look like a crust, some look like leaves, and some look like tiny branches.
copy.tl: May iba't ibang hugis ang lichen: ang iba ay parang manipis na balat, ang iba ay parang dahon, at ang iba ay parang maliliit na sanga.
copy.bis: Adunay nagkalainlaing porma ang lichen: ang uban morag nipis nga panit, ang uban morag dahon, ug ang uban morag gagmayng sanga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bees go through complete metamorphosis: the queen lays eggs, they become larvae fed by worker bees, form pupae, then emerge as adult bees!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a bee life cycle but does not use a flow chart or compare multiple animal life cycles as required by the competency. It provides related content about life cycles but does not directly support the skill of using flow charts to compare stages.

copy.en: Bees go through complete metamorphosis: the queen lays eggs, they become larvae fed by worker bees, form pupae, then emerge as adult bees!
copy.tl: Dumaraan ang bubuyog sa complete metamorphosis: naglalagay ng itlog ang reyna, nagiging larva na pinapakain ng manggagawa, nagiging pupa, at lumalabas bilang adult na bubuyog!
copy.bis: Moagi ang buyog sa complete metamorphosis: mangitlog ang rayna, mahimong larva nga pakan-on sa mga trabahador, mahimong pupa, ug mogawas isip hamtong nga buyog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: egg, larva, pupa, then a biting adult
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a life cycle (egg, larva, pupa, adult) but does not use a flow chart, nor does it compare stages across animals as required by the competency. It only states the mosquito's stages in text, so it does not directly support the skill of using flow charts to compare life-cycle stages.

copy.en: The dengue-carrying Aedes mosquito completes its whole life cycle in just 7 to 10 days in standing water — egg, larva, pupa, then a biting adult!
copy.tl: Ang Aedes mosquito na may dalang dengue ay kumukumpleto ng buong buhay nito sa loob lang ng 7 hanggang 10 araw sa nakatayong tubig — itlog, larva, pupa, tapos adult na lamok na kumakagat!
copy.bis: Ang Aedes mosquito nga may dalang dengue makakumpleto sa tibuok niyang kinabuhi sulod ra sa 7 ngadto sa 10 ka adlaw sa nagtindog nga tubig — itlog, larva, pupa, dayon hamtong nga lamok nga mokagat!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: after spawning, most Pacific salmon die
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions spawning and death, which are life-cycle events, but it does not use a flow chart to compare stages of an animal life cycle, and it does not cover the required examples or stage-by-stage comparison.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: after spawning, most Pacific salmon die
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about salmon, a fish, and only mentions spawning and death. The competency specifically requires comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants from birth/egg/seed to maturity, which this card does not address.

copy.en:
How does a salmon find its way home?

Salmon use their sense of smell to find the river where they were born after years in the ocean — after spawning, most Pacific salmon die.
copy.tl:
Paano nahahanap ng salmon ang daan pauwi?

Ginagamit ng salmon ang kanilang pang-amoy para mahanap ang ilog kung saan sila ipinanganak matapos ang maraming taon sa karagatan — pagkatapos mag-spawn, karamihan sa mga Pacific salmon ay namamatay.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpangita sa salmon sa iyang dalan pauli?

Gigamit sa mga salmon ang ilang pang-amoy aron makit-an ang suba diin sila natawo human sa daghang tuig sa kadagatan — human mag-spawn, ang kadaghanan sa Pacific salmon mangamatay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It bends! This bending is called refraction.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the basic fact that light bends when passing from air into water or glass. The competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with everyday applications. The card provides background knowledge but does not support the investigation, illustration, or use of the specified equipment.

copy.en:
What happens when light passes from air into water or glass?

It bends! This bending is called refraction.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag dumaraan ang liwanag mula sa hangin papuntang tubig o salamin?

Yumuyuko ito! Ang pagyuko na ito ay tinatawag na refraction.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kung moagi ang kahayag gikan sa hangin paingon sa tubig o bubog?

Mabawog kini! Ang pagbawog nga kini gitawag nga refraction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light is the absolute fastest thing in the whole universe!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe electromagnetic radiation (EMR) as energy that is created by the vibrations of electrically charged particles which allows it to travel through materials or space as transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that light is the fastest thing in the universe. It does not describe electromagnetic radiation as energy created by vibrations of electrically charged particles, nor does it mention transverse waves or travel through materials/space. This is a related fact about light but does not directly support the competency's required description.

copy.en:
What is the fastest thing in the whole universe?

Light is the absolute fastest thing in the whole universe!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamabilis na bagay sa buong uniberso?

Ang liwanag ang pinakamabilis na bagay sa buong uniberso!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakapaspas nga butang sa tibuok uniberso?

Ang kahayag mao ang pinakapaspas nga butang sa tibuok uniberso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it makes stars almost impossible to see, and it can confuse animals like newly hatched sea turtles!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes light pollution as harmful to star visibility and to animals, but the competency requires explaining how light and sound can be harmful to people and making suggestions for protection. The card does not address harm to people or any protective suggestions, so it only shares the broad topic of light being harmful.

copy.en: Too much city light at night is called "light pollution" — it makes stars almost impossible to see, and it can confuse animals like newly hatched sea turtles!
copy.tl: Ang sobrang ilaw ng mga lungsod sa gabi ay tinatawag na "light pollution" — dahil dito ay halos hindi na makita ang mga bituin, at nalilito pa ang ilang hayop tulad ng bagong pisang pawikan!
copy.bis: Ang sobra nga kahayag sa mga siyudad sa gabii gitawag og "light pollution" — tungod niini halos dili na makita ang mga bituon, ug malibog pa ang pipila ka hayop sama sa bag-ong napusa nga pawikan!
